blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Digital Payment Systems in India cover various retail payment and settlement mechanisms regulated by the RBI.
NPCI is an initiative of RBI and IBA operating retail payments and settlement systems under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
RBI maintains strict regulatory oversight on private cryptocurrencies while introducing the Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC).
The Account Aggregator (AA) Framework enables secure, consent-based sharing of financial data across financial entities.

blocks.content: NPCI – National Payments Corporation of India
Note: NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India) governs UPI, IMPS, NACH, BBPS, RuPay, FASTag, etc.
10.2 NPCI – National Payments Corporation of India
NPCI was incorporated in 2008 as an umbrella organisation for retail payment systems in India. It is a not-for-profit entity promoted by RBI and IBA (Indian Banks AsGBOciation). Headquarters: Mumbai.

RBI has consistently expressed concern about private cryptocurrencies. The government introduced a Digital Assets Tax (30% flat tax + 1% TDS) in Union Budget 2022-23. RBI launched its own CBDC (Central Bank Digital Currency) called e-Rupee (e-INR) in 2022.

items: NPCI's key innovations including UPI, IMPS, NETC FASTag, and RuPay are frequently tested in competitive exams.
Account Aggregators act strictly as intermediaries for data transfer with consent and cannot store financial data.
Key legal distinction between decentralized cryptocurrencies (not legal tender) and CBDC (sovereign legal tender).
Retail CBDC (Digital Rupee) pilot launched December 2022
e-INR is legal tender; different from cryptocurrency (not decentralised)

blocks.content: Account Aggregator is an RBI-regulated entity that enables seamless and secure sharing of financial data between financial information providers (FIPs) and financial information users (FIUs) with the customer's consent.
